senses.en: to escape or avoid, especially by cleverness or trickery
to avoid giving a direct answer to

ex.en: The senator tried to evade the reporter's question about the budget.
ex.zh: 那位參議員試圖迴避記者關於預算的問題。

root.note: 走出去、溜掉 → 逃避

senses.en: to fade away gradually; to vanish

ex.en: Morning mist will evanesce as soon as the sun rises.
ex.zh: 太陽一升起，晨霧就會漸漸消散。

root.note: 逐漸變空 → 消失

senses.en: quickly fading or disappearing; short-lived

ex.en: The evanescent beauty of cherry blossoms draws huge crowds every spring.
ex.zh: 櫻花轉瞬即逝的美每年春天都吸引大批人潮。

root.note: 逐漸變空的 → 轉瞬即逝的

senses.en: relating to a Protestant tradition stressing personal conversion and the Bible
extremely enthusiastic in promoting a cause

ex.en: She speaks about healthy eating with an almost evangelical passion.
ex.zh: 她談起健康飲食時，帶著近乎傳教般的熱情。

root.note: 好消息（福音）的 → 福音派的

senses.en: a person who seeks to convert others to Christianity
an enthusiastic supporter of something

ex.en: He became an evangelist for electric cars after his first test drive.
ex.zh: 第一次試駕後，他就成了電動車的熱心推廣者。

root.note: 傳播好消息的人 → 傳福音者

senses.en: the act of escaping or avoiding something, especially a duty
an indirect or misleading answer

ex.en: The company was fined millions for tax evasion.
ex.zh: 這家公司因逃稅被罰了數百萬。

root.note: 走出去、溜掉 → 逃避

senses.en: happening at the end of a process or period of time

ex.en: Few people predicted the team's eventual victory in the finals.
ex.zh: 很少有人預料到這支隊伍最後會在決賽中獲勝。

root.note: 最後出來的結果 → 最終的

senses.en: to turn inside out or outward

ex.en: Surgeons had to evert the eyelid to remove the tiny splinter.
ex.zh: 外科醫師必須把眼瞼翻開，才能取出那根小木刺。

root.note: 向外轉 → 外翻

senses.en: to force someone to leave a property, usually by legal process

ex.en: The landlord threatened to evict the tenants if they did not pay rent.
ex.zh: 房東威脅說如果房客不付房租，就要把他們趕出去。

root.note: （在官司中）打敗對方並把人趕出去 → 驅逐

senses.en: of or providing evidence

ex.en: The blurry photo had little evidential value in court.
ex.zh: 那張模糊的照片在法庭上幾乎沒有證據價值。

root.note: 讓人看得出來的 → 證據的

senses.en: to reveal or show clearly (a feeling or quality)

ex.en: The young pianist did not evince any nervousness on stage.
ex.zh: 那位年輕鋼琴家在台上沒有顯露出一絲緊張。

root.note: 證明出來 → 清楚表明

mn: 別和 evict（驅逐）搞混：evince 是「顯露」。

senses.en: to bring a feeling, memory, or image into the mind

ex.en: The smell of fresh bread can evoke memories of my grandmother's kitchen.
ex.zh: 剛出爐的麵包香能喚起我對祖母廚房的回憶。

root.note: 把東西呼喚出來 → 喚起

senses.en: the process by which species develop from earlier forms over time
gradual development

ex.en: Darwin's theory of evolution changed how scientists viewed life on Earth.
ex.zh: 達爾文的演化論改變了科學家看待地球生命的方式。

root.note: （像捲軸一樣）慢慢展開 → 演化、發展

senses.en: to develop gradually
(of species) to change over generations

ex.en: Over the years, the small startup would evolve into a global company.
ex.zh: 這些年來，那家小新創公司逐步發展成一家跨國企業。

root.note: 慢慢展開 → 發展、演化

senses.en: to describe something as larger, better, or worse than it really is

ex.en: Fishermen tend to exaggerate the size of the fish they caught.
ex.zh: 釣客往往會誇大自己釣到的魚有多大。

root.note: 一直往上堆 → 誇大

senses.en: to irritate or annoy intensely

ex.en: His constant excuses began to exasperate even his most patient teacher.
ex.zh: 他不斷找藉口，連最有耐心的老師都被惹火了。

root.note: 使變得很粗暴 → 激怒

senses.en: to dig out or uncover, especially for archaeological study

ex.en: Archaeologists plan to excavate the ancient city next summer.
ex.zh: 考古學家計畫明年夏天開挖這座古城。

root.note: 挖出空洞 → 挖掘

senses.en: to be greater than a number or amount
to go beyond what is allowed

ex.en: Drivers who exceed the speed limit will be fined.
ex.zh: 超速的駕駛人將被罰款。

root.note: 走出界線 → 超過

senses.en: to be exceptionally good at something

ex.en: Students who excel in math may join the advanced class.
ex.zh: 數學特別優秀的學生可以加入進階班。

root.note: 高出眾人 → 擅長、傑出

senses.en: the quality of being outstanding or extremely good

ex.en: The school has a long tradition of academic excellence.
ex.zh: 這所學校向來以學術卓越著稱。

root.note: 高出眾人 → 卓越

senses.en: a title used for certain high officials, such as ambassadors
senses.zh: 閣下（對大使、總督等的尊稱）

ex.en: The guard bowed and said, "His Excellency will see you now."
ex.zh: 警衛鞠躬說：「大使閣下現在要見您。」

root.note: 地位高出眾人者 → 閣下

senses.en: extremely good; outstanding

ex.en: The restaurant serves excellent food at reasonable prices.
ex.zh: 這家餐廳以合理的價格提供極好的餐點。

root.note: 高出眾人的 → 優秀的

senses.en: a short passage taken from a book, film, or piece of music
[ɛkˋsɝpt] to take a short passage from a longer work

ex.en: The teacher read an excerpt from the novel to spark our interest.
ex.zh: 老師朗讀了小說的一段節錄來引起我們的興趣。

root.note: 摘取出來的部分 → 摘錄

senses.en: an amount that is more than necessary or allowed
[ˋɛksɛs] more than is needed or usual

ex.en: Eating sugar in excess can lead to serious health problems.
ex.zh: 攝取過量的糖可能導致嚴重的健康問題。

root.note: 走出界線 → 過量

senses.en: easily excited or upset

ex.en: The excitable puppy jumped on every visitor who came through the door.
ex.zh: 那隻容易興奮的小狗會撲向每個進門的訪客。

root.note: 容易被喚起情緒的 → 易激動的

senses.en: the act of stimulating; (science) raising to a higher energy state

ex.en: The excitation of electrons by light makes the material glow.
ex.zh: 光激發電子，使這種材料發光。

root.note: 喚起出來 → 刺激、激發

senses.en: a sudden cry or remark expressing strong emotion

ex.en: She let out an exclamation of surprise when she opened the gift.
ex.zh: 她打開禮物時驚喜地叫了一聲。

root.note: 大聲叫出來 → 驚呼

senses.en: to deny access to or keep out
to rule out a possibility

ex.en: The club voted to exclude anyone who broke its safety rules.
ex.zh: 俱樂部投票決定，把違反安全規定的人排除在外。

root.note: 關在外面 → 排除

senses.en: the act of keeping someone or something out

ex.en: The exclusion of women from voting lasted for centuries.
ex.zh: 將女性排除在投票權之外的情形持續了好幾個世紀。

root.note: 關在外面 → 排除

senses.en: an abnormal outgrowth on a body or plant
an ugly or unwanted addition

ex.en: Many residents saw the new parking tower as an excrescence on the old town.
ex.zh: 許多居民覺得新的立體停車場是老城區的一個礙眼贅物。

root.note: 向外長出來的東西 → 贅生物

senses.en: the process of eliminating waste from the body; the waste itself

ex.en: The kidneys play a key role in the excretion of waste.
ex.zh: 腎臟在排泄廢物中扮演關鍵角色。

root.note: 分離出去 → 排泄

senses.en: to cause intense physical or mental pain; to torture

ex.en: The long wait for the test results seemed to excruciate the whole family.
ex.zh: 漫長地等待檢查結果，似乎讓全家人痛苦萬分。

root.note: 釘上十字架般地折磨 → 使極度痛苦

senses.en: a short journey or trip, especially for pleasure
a brief departure from a main topic

ex.en: Our class went on an excursion to the science museum.
ex.zh: 我們班去科學博物館校外教學。

root.note: 跑出去一趟 → 短途旅行

senses.en: able to be forgiven or justified

ex.en: A small mistake on your first day is perfectly excusable.
ex.zh: 第一天上班犯個小錯是完全可以原諒的。

root.note: 能免於指控的 → 可原諒的

senses.en: extremely bad or unpleasant

ex.en: The hotel's service was execrable, and we left a day early.
ex.zh: 那家飯店的服務糟透了，我們提早一天離開。

root.note: 被逐出神聖之外、遭詛咒的 → 極糟的

senses.en: the act of cursing or expressing great loathing

ex.en: The dictator's name became an object of execration after his fall.
ex.zh: 獨裁者垮台後，他的名字成了眾人唾罵的對象。

root.note: 逐出神聖之外 → 詛咒

senses.en: a person appointed to carry out the terms of a will

ex.en: She named her eldest son as the executor of her will.
ex.zh: 她指定長子為遺囑執行人。

root.note: 把事情追到完成的人 → 執行人

senses.en: a critical explanation or interpretation of a text, especially scripture

ex.en: The professor offered a careful exegesis of the ancient poem.
ex.zh: 教授對那首古詩做了仔細的詮釋。

root.note: 把意思引導出來 → 詮釋

senses.en: a person or thing serving as a typical or excellent model

ex.en: The old library is an exemplar of Gothic Revival architecture.
ex.zh: 那座老圖書館是哥德復興式建築的典範。

root.note: 作為例子的東西 → 典範

senses.en: serving as a desirable model; very good
(of punishment) serving as a warning

ex.en: The firefighter received a medal for her exemplary courage.
ex.zh: 那位消防員因堪為表率的勇氣而獲頒獎章。

root.note: 可以當例子的 → 模範的

senses.en: to be a typical example of
to illustrate by giving an example

ex.en: These paintings exemplify the bright colors of the Impressionist style.
ex.zh: 這些畫作正是印象派鮮明色彩的典型代表。

root.note: 使成為例子 → 例證

senses.en: free from an obligation or rule that applies to others
to free from an obligation

ex.en: Students with medical notes are exempt from the swimming test.
ex.zh: 有醫生證明的學生可以免考游泳。

root.note: 被拿出來、不算在內 → 豁免的

senses.en: to apply force, influence, or pressure
to make a strong effort

ex.en: Parents exert a strong influence on their children's habits.
ex.zh: 父母對孩子的習慣有很大的影響力。

parts.m: join, put 放置（拉丁文 serere）

root.note: 把力量放出去 → 施加

senses.en: to breathe out

ex.en: Take a deep breath, hold it, and then slowly exhale.
ex.zh: 深吸一口氣，憋住，然後慢慢吐氣。

root.note: 向外呼氣 → 呼氣

senses.en: to tire out completely
to use up completely
waste gases from an engine

ex.en: If we keep spending like this, we will exhaust our savings by June.
ex.zh: 如果我們繼續這樣花錢，六月前就會把積蓄用光。

root.note: 汲取到見底 → 耗盡

senses.en: able to be used up completely

ex.en: Coal and oil are exhaustible resources that will not last forever.
ex.zh: 煤和石油是會耗盡的資源，不會永遠存在。

root.note: 可以被汲取到見底的 → 可耗盡的

senses.en: a state of extreme tiredness
the act of using something up

ex.en: After running the marathon, she collapsed from exhaustion.
ex.zh: 跑完馬拉松後，她累到虛脫倒下。

root.note: 被汲取到見底 → 筋疲力盡

senses.en: including every possible detail; thorough

ex.en: The police conducted an exhaustive search of the forest.
ex.zh: 警方對森林進行了地毯式的搜索。

root.note: 把所有東西都汲取出來的 → 詳盡的

mn: exhaustive 是「詳盡的」，不是 exhausting（令人疲憊的）。

senses.en: to make someone feel very happy, animated, or elated

ex.en: A fast ride down the snowy slope never fails to exhilarate him.
ex.zh: 從雪坡上飛速滑下總是讓他興奮不已。

root.note: 使非常快樂 → 使振奮

senses.en: to dig up a buried body
to bring something forgotten back to attention

ex.en: The court ordered officials to exhume the body for a new autopsy.
ex.zh: 法院下令官員開棺驗屍重新解剖。

root.note: 從土裡挖出來 → 掘墓

senses.en: an urgent need or demand

ex.en: The hospital must be ready for every exigency, from floods to power cuts.
ex.zh: 醫院必須為各種緊急狀況做好準備，從水災到停電都是。

root.note: 驅使人非做不可 → 急迫需要

senses.en: pressing; demanding immediate attention
requiring much effort; demanding

ex.en: Police may enter a home without a warrant in exigent circumstances.
ex.zh: 在緊急情況下，警方可以無搜索票進入民宅。

root.note: 驅使人立即行動的 → 緊急的

senses.en: the fact or state of being real or alive
a way of living

ex.en: Scientists debate the existence of life on other planets.
ex.zh: 科學家爭論其他星球上是否存在生命。

root.note: 站出來、顯現出來 → 存在

senses.en: a way out of a place
to go out of or leave

ex.en: Please use the nearest exit in case of fire.
ex.zh: 發生火災時，請使用最近的出口。

root.note: 走出去 → 出口

senses.en: a mass departure of people

ex.en: Rising rents caused an exodus of young families from the city.
ex.zh: 房租上漲導致年輕家庭大批離開這座城市。

root.note: 走上出去的路 → 大批出走

mn: 聖經《出埃及記》就叫 Exodus。

senses.en: to officially declare someone free from blame

ex.en: New DNA evidence helped exonerate the man after ten years in prison.
ex.zh: 新的 DNA 證據幫這名入獄十年的男子洗清了罪名。

root.note: 卸下負擔 → 免除罪責

senses.en: the quality of being unreasonably high, especially in price

ex.en: Travelers complained about the exorbitance of airport food prices.
ex.zh: 旅客抱怨機場的餐點價格貴得離譜。

root.note: 偏離軌道 → 過分

senses.en: (of a price or amount) unreasonably high

ex.en: We refused to pay the exorbitant fee for a bottle of water.
ex.zh: 我們拒絕為一瓶水付那麼離譜的價錢。

root.note: 偏離正常軌道的 → 過高的

senses.en: to drive out an evil spirit
to get rid of an unpleasant memory or feeling
senses.zh: 擺脫（不愉快的記憶、情緒）

ex.en: Writing the memoir helped her exorcise the painful memories of the war.
ex.zh: 寫回憶錄幫助她擺脫了戰爭的痛苦記憶。

root.note: 以誓言命令（邪靈）出去 → 驅魔

senses.en: originating in or typical of a distant foreign country
attractive because unusual

ex.en: The market sells exotic fruits from Southeast Asia.
ex.zh: 這個市場販賣來自東南亞的異國水果。

root.note: 來自外面的 → 異國的

senses.en: to become or make larger
to give more details about

ex.en: The company plans to expand into Japan next year.
ex.zh: 這家公司計畫明年拓展到日本市場。

root.note: 向外展開 → 擴大

senses.en: a wide, open area of land, sea, or sky

ex.en: From the plane we saw a vast expanse of desert.
ex.zh: 從飛機上我們看到一大片廣闊的沙漠。

root.note: 向外展開的一片 → 廣闊區域

senses.en: the act of becoming larger or more extensive

ex.en: The rapid expansion of the city put pressure on its water supply.
ex.zh: 城市的迅速擴張對供水造成壓力。

root.note: 向外展開 → 擴張

senses.en: a person who lives outside their native country
[ɛksˋpetrɪˏet] to leave or expel from one's native country

ex.en: As an expatriate in Tokyo, he often missed Taiwanese food.
ex.zh: 身為旅居東京的外國人，他常常想念台灣菜。

root.note: 離開祖國的人 → 旅居國外者

senses.en: to believe that something will happen
to require something as appropriate

ex.en: We expect the package to arrive on Friday.
ex.zh: 我們預計包裹會在週五送達。

root.note: 向外張望等待 → 期待

senses.en: the state of expecting something, especially something pleasant
the expected length of something (e.g., life expectancy)

ex.en: Life expectancy in Taiwan has risen steadily over the past fifty years.
ex.zh: 台灣的平均壽命在過去五十年來穩定上升。

root.note: 向外張望等待 → 期待

senses.en: to cough up and spit out phlegm

ex.en: The doctor asked the patient to expectorate into a small cup.
ex.zh: 醫生要病人把痰咳到小杯子裡。

root.note: 從胸腔弄出來 → 咳痰

senses.en: the quality of being convenient and practical, even if improper or immoral
senses.zh: 權宜之計；（不顧原則的）方便行事

ex.en: The mayor was accused of choosing political expediency over principle.
ex.zh: 市長被指控為了政治上的方便而犧牲原則。

root.note: 把腳從束縛中解開、行動方便 → 權宜

senses.en: convenient and practical, though possibly improper
a means of achieving an end, often a temporary one

ex.en: It was more expedient to hire a taxi than to wait for the bus.
ex.zh: 叫計程車比等公車方便多了。

root.note: 讓腳自由行動的 → 方便的

senses.en: to make a process happen faster

ex.en: Paying an extra fee will expedite the passport application.
ex.zh: 多付一筆費用可以加快護照申請的速度。

root.note: 把腳從束縛中解開 → 使加速

senses.en: done with speed and efficiency

ex.en: The team found an expeditious way to process the refunds.
ex.zh: 團隊找到一個迅速處理退款的方法。

root.note: 腳步自由、行動快的 → 迅速的

senses.en: to spend or use up time, money, or energy
senses.zh: 花費；耗費（時間、金錢、精力）

ex.en: Don't expend all your energy in the first lap of the race.
ex.zh: 別在比賽的第一圈就把力氣用光。

root.note: 把錢秤出去 → 花費

senses.en: the cost of something; money spent
something given up for a result (at the expense of)

ex.en: He succeeded at work but at the expense of his health.
ex.zh: 他在工作上成功了，卻犧牲了健康。

root.note: 付出去的錢 → 費用

senses.en: to make amends for guilt or wrongdoing

ex.en: He volunteered for years, hoping to expiate the harm he had caused.
ex.zh: 他當了好幾年志工，希望彌補自己造成的傷害。

root.note: 用虔誠的行為把罪清出去 → 贖罪

senses.en: to analyze and explain in detail

ex.en: The essay asks students to explicate a short poem line by line.
ex.zh: 這篇作文要學生逐行解析一首短詩。

root.note: 把摺起來的東西攤開 → 闡明

senses.en: stated clearly and in detail, leaving no room for confusion
showing sexual or violent content openly

ex.en: The teacher gave explicit instructions about how to cite sources.
ex.zh: 老師給了關於如何引用資料的明確指示。

root.note: 攤開來擺明的 → 明確的

senses.en: to burst violently
to increase suddenly and rapidly
to show sudden strong emotion

ex.en: Fireworks explode over the harbor every New Year's Eve.
ex.zh: 每年跨年夜，煙火都會在港口上空綻放。

root.note: 原指拍手把演員轟下台 → 引申為爆開

senses.en: a violent bursting with noise
a sudden large increase

ex.en: The explosion shattered windows three blocks away.
ex.zh: 這場爆炸震碎了三條街外的窗戶。

root.note: 向外爆開 → 爆炸

senses.en: able or likely to explode
likely to cause strong emotions or conflict
senses.zh: 一觸即發的；易引起爭議的

senses.en: a substance that can explode

ex.en: Immigration remains an explosive issue in the election.
ex.zh: 移民問題在這次選舉中仍是一觸即發的議題。

root.note: 會向外爆開的 → 爆炸性的

senses.en: a detailed explanation of a theory or idea
a large public exhibition

ex.en: The first chapter is a clear exposition of the author's main argument.
ex.zh: 第一章清楚闡述了作者的主要論點。

root.note: 把東西擺出來給人看 → 說明、展覽

senses.en: intended to explain or describe something

ex.en: An expository essay explains a topic using facts rather than opinions.
ex.zh: 說明文是用事實而非意見來解釋一個主題。

root.note: 把道理擺出來的 → 說明性的

senses.en: to express strong disagreement or protest

ex.en: She tried to expostulate with the referee, but he ignored her.
ex.zh: 她試圖跟裁判據理力爭，但裁判不理她。

root.note: 強烈地要求 → 抗議、勸誡

senses.en: the state of being unprotected from something harmful
public attention or publicity

ex.en: Long exposure to loud music can damage your hearing.
ex.zh: 長時間接觸大聲的音樂會損害聽力。

root.note: 被放在外面 → 暴露

senses.en: effectively showing thought or feeling
senses.zh: 富於表現力的；表情豐富的

ex.en: The actor has an expressive face that shows every emotion.
ex.zh: 那位演員表情豐富，每種情緒都寫在臉上。

root.note: 把感受擠壓出來的 → 富表現力的

senses.en: the act of forcing someone to leave a place or organization

ex.en: Cheating on the final exam could result in expulsion from the school.
ex.zh: 期末考作弊可能會被學校開除。

root.note: 推出去 → 驅逐

senses.en: still in existence; surviving

ex.en: Only three copies of the original manuscript are still extant.
ex.zh: 原始手稿只剩下三份存世。

root.note: 還站在那裡的 → 現存的

mn: extant（現存的）與 extinct（滅絕的）意思相反，別搞混。

senses.en: spoken or done without preparation

ex.en: His extemporaneous speech at the wedding made everyone laugh.
ex.zh: 他在婚禮上的即興致詞逗得大家哈哈大笑。

root.note: 出於當下那個時刻的 → 即興的

senses.en: without planning or preparation
spoken or done without preparation

ex.en: The mayor spoke extempore when the microphone failed and her notes blew away.
ex.zh: 麥克風故障、講稿又被風吹走時，市長只好即席發言。

root.note: 出於當下（拉丁文 ex tempore）→ 即席地

senses.en: able to be extended or stretched

ex.en: The software is extensible, so users can add their own features.
ex.zh: 這套軟體可擴充，使用者能加入自己的功能。

root.note: 能向外伸展的 → 可延伸的

senses.en: an additional period of time
an added part that makes something larger
a telephone line within a building

ex.en: The professor granted me a one-week extension on my paper.
ex.zh: 教授答應讓我的報告延一週交。

root.note: 向外伸展 → 延長

senses.en: covering a large area or amount; wide-ranging

ex.en: The storm caused extensive damage along the coast.
ex.zh: 暴風雨沿著海岸造成大規模的破壞。

root.note: 向外伸展很遠的 → 廣泛的

senses.en: a muscle that straightens or extends a part of the body

ex.en: The extensor in your forearm straightens your fingers.
ex.zh: 前臂的伸肌負責把手指伸直。

root.note: 使肢體伸展的東西 → 伸肌

senses.en: to make a wrong seem less serious by giving an excuse

ex.en: Nothing can extenuate his decision to drive after drinking.
ex.zh: 他酒後開車的決定沒有任何理由可以開脫。

root.note: 使變薄 → 減輕（罪過）

mn: 常見片語 extenuating circumstances（情有可原的情況）。

senses.en: the outer surface or structure
situated on the outside

ex.en: Beneath his tough exterior, he is actually very kind.
ex.zh: 在他強硬的外表下，其實是個非常善良的人。

root.note: 較外面的 → 外部

senses.en: belonging to or on the outside
coming from outside an organization or country

ex.en: The company hired an external auditor to review its accounts.
ex.zh: 公司聘請外部審計人員來審查帳目。

root.note: 在外面的 → 外部的

senses.en: (of a species) no longer existing
(of a volcano) no longer active

ex.en: Dinosaurs became extinct about 66 million years ago.
ex.zh: 恐龍大約在六千六百萬年前滅絕。

root.note: 火被熄滅 → 滅絕的

senses.en: to put out a fire or light
to end or destroy (a hope, feeling)

ex.en: Firefighters worked all night to extinguish the blaze.
ex.zh: 消防員整夜奮戰撲滅大火。

root.note: 把火弄熄 → 撲滅

senses.en: to praise enthusiastically

ex.en: Health experts often extol the benefits of regular exercise.
ex.zh: 健康專家經常大力讚揚規律運動的好處。

root.note: 把人高高舉起 → 讚揚

senses.en: to obtain something by force, threats, or other unfair means

ex.en: The gang tried to extort money from local shop owners.
ex.zh: 那個幫派試圖向當地店家勒索錢財。

root.note: 扭出來 → 勒索

senses.en: the crime of obtaining money through threats or force

ex.en: The official was arrested on charges of extortion and bribery.
ex.zh: 那名官員因涉嫌勒索和賄賂而被捕。

root.note: 扭出來 → 勒索
